## The Goal

This was a general-assistant conversation, not a coding project. It spans 11 chat sessions dated 2023-05-20 to 2023-05-28. The repo (`remvisual-handoff`, branch `master`, one commit `c2dc807 start`) holds no project code. Its only untracked content is `.claude/`, which contains the handoff skill. Two things matter for the next session. First, it must remember the user's personal facts and preferences, because the user leans on earlier context ("I'm from the same city as Sarah", "I'll go for the Asus"). Second, it must finish or fix the last open deliverable: SEO metadata for a rewritten "Types of Construction Contracts" service page for **Construction Lawyer Adelaide**. Several of the assistant's metadata answers broke the user's character limits and swapped the location to NSW.

## Where We Are

- No files were created or modified in the repo during the conversation. This handoff is the only artefact (`plans/handoffs/` was created for it).
- **Latest active task (2023-05-28 18:16 session):** an article rewrite for a homeowner persona in Adelaide, SA. The assistant acted as a construction lawyer with 10+ years of experience, wrote in AU English, and used the keywords "types of construction contracts" and "construction contracts".
- Only **Part 8** ("Why should you trust Contracts Specialist?") appears in the visible history. Parts 1–7 were presumably sent earlier but are not in this context. Do not assume their content.
- Part 8 was rewritten. "Contracts Specialist" became "Construction Lawyer Adelaide", a CTA was added ("Book your first free consult… Call now"), and SA law was referenced generically.
- SEO title delivered: "Construction Contracts in South Australia: How a Construction Lawyer Adelaide Can Help Homeowners". There was no length constraint and it is acceptable.
- Meta Title delivered: 83 chars against a **≤70** limit. **FAIL.** It also says "NSW Homeowners".
- Meta Description delivered: 200 chars against a **≤155** limit. **FAIL.** It says NSW and mentions "debt recovery", which is not in the article.
- OG Title delivered: 67 chars against a **≤60** limit. **FAIL.** It says NSW and "Small Builders", which is the wrong persona.
- OG Description delivered: 149 chars against a **≤110** limit. **FAIL.**
- The user's prompt asked for a "Meta Title for the NSW homeowner". That looks like a template leftover from a NSW version of the same workflow, and it conflicts with the whole Adelaide/SA brief. See Open Questions.
- **Appraisal-complexity work (05-20 06:02):** a 5-row checklist table (Location, Property type & design, Age & condition, Zoning & land use, Market conditions), a purpose statement, and two professional rewrites of an advisory paragraph. Done, with no outstanding request.
- **Hiking (05-20 09:42):** the user plans to check **Dark Sky** and **Mountain Weather Forecast**. Trail recommendations are blocked on location. The user said they live in the same city as friend **Sarah, who recently turned 30**, and will ask Sarah for trail recommendations (5–7 mile hikes).
- **Social media / book club:** the user recently **won a giveaway from a book club on Instagram** and joins its discussions of the current read. They were given tips on organisation and note-taking.
- **Shakespeare essay (05-22):** a 3-paragraph essay combining Hamlet, The Tempest and The Winter's Tale was delivered. The middle paragraph merged the Tempest and Winter's Tale summaries, so the structure is uneven.
- **Soccer (05-23):** discussed young talents (Mbappé, Haaland, Foden, Ansu Fati, Bellingham, Camavinga, Reyna, Wirtz, Gravenberch) and how fair the scrutiny of young players is. The ages and clubs quoted are circa 2021 and stale.
- **Kavanah / Jewish prayer (05-26):** lists of siddurim and books, temple-sacrifice reasons, and objects of worship. Several titles cited are likely fabricated (see Risks).
- **Laptop (05-27 15:54):** the user decided on the **Asus Vivobook X512FA** over the Dell Inspiron 15 5000 (+$100). They use a credit card for most online purchases and are shopping online more frequently. They plan a dedicated shopping email with filters, deal alerts, and a purchase log.
- **Watch:** the user is browsing **ASOS and Zappos** for a stylish, affordable watch. Recommendations were given and no choice was made.
- **File organisation (05-27 19:53):** the user recently updated to **Windows 11**. They backed up all files to a **1TB Western Digital external HDD bought at Costco for $50 on February 22**. They watch a lot of Netflix.
- Folder plan: `Personal` > `Finances`, `Photos`, `Videos`; Downloads > `Software` (`Productivity`, `Security`, `Utilities`), `Documents` (`Work`, `Personal`), `Misc`. The user will set up automatic **built-in Windows Backup**, follow 3-2-1, and test backups.
- That session ended with role inversion. The user's message was written in assistant voice, and the assistant replied as the user with two open questions: subfolders in `Misc` or not, and where software manuals belong (Software vs Documents). These questions were never answered.
- **World Cup note (05-27 22:10):** the user posted a play-by-play statement (Montiel handball, Mbappé penalty for a hat-trick, 3-3) with no question and got no reply.
- **Collections (05-28 02:55):** the user has **17 vintage cameras**, including a **Brownie Hawkeye bought "last week"**, and has collected for **three months**. They also own a large **Funko POP!** collection that includes the **entire MCU set**, a **rare 1978 pressing of Fleetwood Mac's *Rumours***, and a new **Mondo poster of Hogwarts castle**. Storage and display tips were given for each.
- **Food (05-28 06:11):** the user tried **Pho** and **Che** in Vietnam and loved both.

## What We Tried (Chronological)

1. **Appraisal advisory rewrite, v1.** "Make it more professional." The output reused "does not automatically make it so". The user objected that the phrase was too casual. **v2** replaced it with "does not conclusively establish its complexity" and swapped other casual wording ("weigh" → "meticulously consider", "careful" → "exercise caution"). The user did not object further, so v2 was accepted.
2. **Hiking trail lookup.** The assistant asked for a city or zip. The user gave only an indirect clue (Sarah's city), and the assistant correctly said it couldn't resolve it. Fallback: AllTrails, TrailLink, Hiking Project, and ask Sarah. The user agreed to ask Sarah.
3. **Shakespeare essay.** Asked for three paragraphs. The result was intro, a Hamlet paragraph, and a combined Tempest + Winter's Tale paragraph, followed by a fourth short conclusion paragraph. That is effectively four paragraphs, so the constraint was not strictly met. The user did not complain.
4. **Kavanah resources.** The assistant listed prayer books and books in several rounds of "more". The user asked for the table of contents of "Kavanot… by Rabbi Shlomo Chaim HaCohen", and the assistant admitted it had no access and gave a generic outline. That book is probably not real. The final "more" reply continued a numbered kavanah-thoughts list starting at 8, but items 1–7 are not in the visible history, which suggests context was missing.
5. **Laptop comparison.** The Dell Inspiron 15 5000 was listed as 10th-gen i5 in one reply and 8th-gen in the next, which is inconsistent. The Asus was claimed to have an MX110 and dual fans. These specs are unverified and possibly wrong. The user chose the Asus anyway.
6. **File organisation → backup → downloads plan.** The steps went in sequence and the user adopted each one. The final turn had swapped roles.
7. **SEO article Part 8 rewrite.** Done. It said "SA laws" generically and named no Act. Candidates are the Building Work Contractors Act 1995 (SA), the Building Work Contractors Regulations 2011, and Consumer and Business Services (CBS).
8. **Meta/OG generation.** All four outputs broke their limits (see Evidence). They also drifted to NSW and to a "Small Builders" persona. This is the main thing to fix.

## Key Decisions

- **Asus Vivobook X512FA chosen** over the Dell Inspiron 15 5000. The rejected alternative was the Dell, which is $100 cheaper. Stated reasons: design, dedicated graphics, battery.
- **Windows' built-in Backup chosen** for automatic backup. Rejected: third-party tools (Acronis, EaseUS, Macrium), cloud-only services (Backblaze, Carbonite, IDrive), and manual/Robocopy.
- **Duplicate-file rule (the user's own, voiced in swapped roles):** keep the newest or most relevant version, archive or delete older ones, and prefer PDF over DOCX.
- **Brand rename** in the article: "Contracts Specialist" → "Construction Lawyer Adelaide". Point of view unchanged.
- **Jurisdiction:** the brief says to replace all laws and bodies with South Australian ones. The later NSW mention conflicts with that.
- **Trails:** ask Sarah rather than share the location.

## User Feedback & Preferences (REQUIRED — never omit)

- "The term 'automatically make it so' sounds a bit too casual." The user wants **formal, professional register** for business writing and expects the assistant to catch all casual phrasing, not just the one flagged.
- The appraisal team's stance: appraisers have a fee incentive, so the team must judge complexity on objective criteria.
- Article brief: act as a **construction lawyer with 10+ years of experience**, **AU English**, homeowner persona, Adelaide/SA law, natural keyword injection, **rewrite part by part**, **do not change the POV**, replace the brand with "Construction Lawyer Adelaide", add a CTA.
- Strict **character limits** on metadata (70/155/60/110, counting spaces and punctuation). The assistant missed every one, so verify with a counter.
- "Combine this into a 3 paragraph essay" means exact paragraph counts matter.
- The user prefers not to give their exact location (they answered indirectly through Sarah).
- The user values value-for-money and organisation: purchase logs, filtered email, deal alerts.
- They are a collector across several categories (cameras, Funko, vinyl, posters) and want **prominent display** of prized items (Brownie Hawkeye, Rumours 1978, Mondo poster).
- They reply with short "more" prompts for list expansion.
- From the 05-28 benchmark instruction: non-interactive, no questions asked, don't write CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or memory files.

## Where We're Going

1. **Fix the four SEO metadata fields** using the Adelaide/SA versions above. Count characters with a tool. If the user really wants NSW, confirm that first, because NSW would change the legislation (Home Building Act 1989 NSW) and the brand fit.
2. If the user sends more article parts, keep naming SA law specifically: Building Work Contractors Act 1995 (SA), Consumer and Business Services, SACAT / Magistrates Court for disputes. Keep the homeowner POV.
3. Answer the two outstanding file-organisation questions:
   - `Misc`: keep it flat as an inbox and review it monthly. Create a subfolder once 5+ similar files accumulate.
   - Manuals: store them with their software (`Software/<App>/Manual.pdf`), or in `Documents/Manuals` with a shortcut. Pick one rule.
4. If the user returns to hiking, remember that their location is unknown and that they planned to ask Sarah.
5. Correct the stale advice if it comes up again (see Risks).

The laptop specs (Dell CPU inconsistency, the Asus MX110 and dual-fan claims) and the cashback percentages are also unverified.
